Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”) [1]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,[2]
notice is hereby given that on October 9, 2026, CME Securities Clearing Inc. (“CMESC”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been substantially prepared by CMESC. CMESC filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act.[3]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. CMESC's Statement of the Terms and Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
(a) The proposed rule change of CME Securities Clearing Inc. (“CMESC”) is provided in Exhibit 5. The proposed rule change includes amendments to the CMESC Risk Management Framework (“RMF”) related to CMESC's default management practices, which provides for necessary transparency to and clarity for CMESC staff in managing a default.[4]
Each modification is described in more detail below.
II. CMESC's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, CMESC included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. CMESC has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. CMESC's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
Background
CMESC's default management procedures cover the management of a default of either a Member or User (collectively, “Participants”) and are designed to ensure the continuity of CMESC's clearance and settlement functions and particularly, the ongoing maintenance of the services provided to non-defaulting Participants, while supporting market integrity and minimizing market disruptions. The primary purpose of the proposed rule change is to enhance the default management process by further codifying the documentation of the default management procedures in the RMF. In particular, the proposed rule change would amend the RMF to (i) provide additional detail around arrangements involving a third-party liquidation agent for managing a Participant default, and (ii) make certain clarifying and administrative changes, where appropriate, in the RMF; and (iii) to clarify the role of CMESC's Risk Management Committee (“CSRMC”) in designing the default management procedures.
Liquidation Agent and Execution Brokers
Section 14.1.1 (“Participant Default Management Process”) of the RMF would be amended to specify that the close-out process of a defaulted Participant's portfolio may include the use of a liquidation agent and one or more execution brokers.[5]
Broadly, the amended RMF would provide that, in managing a default, CMESC and any liquidation agent will collaborate to assess the exposures of the defaulted Participant's portfolio, including associated settlement obligations as they come due, and formulate a close-out strategy under the prevailing market conditions to minimize potential losses and market disruptions and to support market integrity. More specifically, the amended RMF would describe the expectations for a third-party liquidation agent, if used, to assist CMESC with designing and executing the close-out strategy for the defaulted Participant's portfolio. In accordance with the amended RMF, the liquidation agent will be expected to coordinate with CMESC to reconcile positions of the defaulted Participant and assess the outstanding exposure of the defaulted Participant over the course of managing the default.
The amended RMF also would provide that the liquidation agent may use various methods to execute close-out trades, including, but not limited to, executing open market transactions; enter into hedging transactions to mitigate the risk of the defaulted Participant's portfolio; and perform other related tasks appropriate to assist CMESC in managing the risk from the Participant's default. In addition, Section 14.1.1 of the RMF would recognize that CMESC may engage one or more execution brokers to coordinate with the liquidation agent and CMESC to provide certain operational services related to the close-out trades arranged or executed by the liquidation agent in managing a default. The amended RMF would include new language to specify that, where appropriate, CMESC would maintain an account with the execution broker where it would be the principal, and the execution broker may submit back-to-back trades that mirror the liquidation agent's close-out trades. CMESC would further specify in the RMF that the submission of back-to-back trades is expected to ensure that CMESC's account at the execution broker maintains a net flat position and facilitate CMESC's ability to meet the settlement obligations of the defaulted Participant as they come due.

October 16, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),[1]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,[2]
notice is hereby given that on October 13, 2026, Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act [3]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.[4]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe EDGX” or the “Exchange”) is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission” or “SEC”) a proposed rule change to amend Rule 11.1(a)(3) to describe when unpriced orders are eligible for execution and to amend Rule 11.6(q)(2) to clarify the expiration of Day Orders entered during the Overnight Trading Session or Order Acceptance Queueing Time. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.1(a)(3) to introduce rule text to describe when orders that do not contain a limit price are eligible for execution. Under current Rule 11.1(a)(1), the Exchange does not accept Market Orders,[5]
other than those with a Time-in-Force (“TIF”) instruction of Regular Hours Only [6]
or a Stop Price, prior to 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time or prior to 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time for orders eligible for a 7:00 a.m. Start.[7]
As part of the Exchange's transition to trading 23 hours per day, 5 days per week (“23x5 Trading”), the Exchange updated Rule 11.1(a) to introduce a new subparagraph (3) titled “Orders Permitted in Each Session.” [8]
Rule 11.1(a)(3), which is approved but not yet effective, states: “Market Orders, other than those designated with a Time-in-Force instruction of Regular Hours Only or those that include a Stop Price, will not be accepted by the Exchange prior to Regular Trading Hours.” The intent of this sentence was to prevent Market Orders from executing during the Overnight Trading Session [9]
and the Pre-Opening Session,[10]
but the text did not expressly prohibit the Exchange from accepting Market Orders during Regular Trading Hours and executing during the Post-Closing Session,[11]
which experiences similar characteristics regarding liquidity and volume as the current Early Trading Session.[12]
Now, the Exchange proposes to add an additional sentence to the end of Rule 11.1(a)(3) which states: “Orders without a limit price will not be eligible for execution outside of Regular Trading Hours.” The addition of this sentence eliminates any potential ambiguity about when an order that does not contain a limit price will be eligible for execution on the Exchange. In addition, this proposed change is substantially similar to limits on unpriced orders currently in place on Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) and NYSE Arca, Inc. (“NYSE Arca”) and differs only in that the Exchange's proposed rule refers to orders without a limit price rather than specifically designating market orders or pegged orders as other market centers have done in their rule text.[13]
The Exchange also proposes to amend Rule 11.6(q)(2) to clarify that a Day Order entered during the Order Acceptance Queueing Time [14]
or Overnight Trading Session will expire at the end of Regular Trading Hours on the same business day to which the Overnight Trading Session belongs, as provided in Rule 11.1(b).[15]
This amendment replaces the phrase “following trading day,” which could be read ambiguously for orders entered after midnight during the Overnight Trading Session, with language that expressly ties the order's expiration to the business day to which the Overnight Trading Session belongs.
The change is consistent with the Exchange's intent as described in the Original Filing, which introduced the 23x5 Trading framework and explained that “a trading day is deemed to begin at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the preceding calendar day.” Under Rule 11.1(b), a business day includes the Overnight Trading Session on the preceding calendar day, meaning the entire Overnight Trading Session (from 9:00 p.m. through 4:00 a.m.) belongs to the following business day. The proposed amendment merely conforms the Day Order TIF definition to this structural principle and does not alter any operational aspect of Day Order handling.
Specifically, current Rule 11.6(q)(2) provides that a Day Order entered during the Order Acceptance Queueing Time or the Overnight Trading Session “will expire at the end of Regular Trading Hours on the following trading day.” The Exchange proposes to replace “following trading day” with “same business day to which the Overnight Trading Session belongs, as provided in Rule 11.1(b).” This revision eliminates any potential ambiguity regarding whether an order entered after midnight
i.e.,
during the portion of the Overnight Trading Session occurring on a new calendar day) could be interpreted as expiring on a different business day than intended.

In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.

Title:

Abstract:
Section 25F of the Internal Revenue Code (IRC) allows States to voluntarily elect to participate in the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) program. States must provide the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) with a list of the scholarship granting organizations (SGOs) located in their State that meet the requirements of IRC section 25F(c)(5). Form 15714 provides an authorized State representative with a method to elect participation under IRC section 25F. Revenue Procedure 2026-6 provides guidance regarding a procedure for a State to voluntarily elect to participate under IRC section 25F. T.D. 10057 provides rules for State elections to participate under section 25F, including the registration process on the IRS State section 25F portal; rules for information and certifications a State is required to provide for each organization included on the State SGO list; and procedures a State must use in determining whether organizations meet the requirements of section 25F(c)(5). In addition, T.D. 10057 provides procedures for registering SGOs through an IRS electronic SGO portal; reporting, recordkeeping, and third-party disclosure of qualified contributions received by SGOs; and providing timely written acknowledgments to donors.

AGENCY:
Bureau of Indian Affairs, Interior.
                    SUMMARY:
The Department of the Interior (Department) gives notice that the group known as the Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation, a petitioner for Federal acknowledgment as an American Indian Tribe, has chosen to complete the petitioning process under the current version of the acknowledgment regulations and has supplemented its petition. The Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation had been proceeding under a previous version of the regulations (as they existed prior to July 31, 2015). The Department seeks comments and evidence from the public on the supplemented petition.
                    DATES:
Comments and evidence must be postmarked by February 18, 2027.
                    ADDRESSES:
                        Copies of the narrative portion(s) of the supplemented documented petition, as submitted by the petitioner (with any redactions appropriate under 25 CFR 83.21(b)), and other information are available at the Office of Federal Acknowledgement's (OFA) website: 
                        www.bia.gov/as-ia/ofa.
                         Submit any comments or evidence to: Department of the Interior, Office of the Assistant Secretary—Indian Affairs, Attention: Office of Federal acknowledgment, Mail Stop 4071 MIB, 1849 C Street NW, Washington, DC 20240, or by email to: 
                        Ofa_Info@bia.gov.
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation submitted a documented petition on February 24, 1988, for evaluation under a previous version of the acknowledgment regulations (as they existed prior to July 31, 2015). On July 1, 2015, the Department revised 25 CFR part 83 (80 FR 37862), and the regulations became final and effective on July 31, 2015. Pursuant to 25 CFR 83.7 of the revised regulations, the Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation chose to complete the petitioning process under the revised regulations and has now supplemented its petition.
A key goal of the 2015 revisions was to improve transparency through increased notice of petitions and providing improved public access to petitions. The Department informs the public that the petition submitted by the Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation, which has not yet received a final agency decision, will be evaluated pursuant to the standards and processes set forth in the current regulations. Portions of the supplemented petition are publicly available on the website identified above for easy access, and OFA seeks public comment on the petition.
The contact information for the petitioner is Mr. Nathan Banda, 31411 LaMatanza St., Ste. A, San Juan Capistrano, CA 92675.
Also, OFA publishes on its website the following:
i. The narrative portion(s) of the supplemented documented petition, as submitted by the petitioner (with any redactions appropriate under 25 CFR 83.21(b));
ii. The name, location, and mailing address of the petitioner and other information to identify the entity;
iii. The date of receipt;
iv. The opportunity for individuals and entities to submit comments and evidence supporting or opposing the petitioner's request for acknowledgment within 120 days of the date of the website posting; and
v. The opportunity for individuals and entities to request to be kept informed of general actions regarding a specific petitioner.
Authority
The Department publishes this notice and request for comment in the exercise of authority delegated by the Secretary of the Interior to the Assistant Secretary—Indian Affairs by Department Manual part 209, chapter 8.
                    William Henry Kirkland III,
Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs.

Pursuant to the Act of August 15, 1953, Public Law 83-277, 67 Stat. 586, 18 U.S.C. 1161, as interpreted by the Supreme Court in

463 U.S. 713 (1983), the Secretary of the Interior shall certify and publish in the

On May 6, 2026, Ohkay Owingeh, located in New Mexico, through Resolution No. 2026-33, adopted this amended Liquor Control Ordinance, which regulates and controls the consumption, possession, production, and sale of alcoholic beverages within the Pueblo's territorial jurisdiction.
This notice is published in accordance with the authority delegated by the Secretary of the Interior to the Assistant Secretary—Indian Affairs. I certify that Ohkay Owingeh, New Mexico duly adopted this amendment to the Pueblo's Liquor Control Ordinance by Resolution No. 2026-33 on May 6, 2026.
The Ohkay Owingeh, New Mexico Liquor Control Ordinance, as amended, shall read as follows:
Ohkay Owingeh Amended Liquor Control Ordinance
Section 1—Title
This Ordinance shall be known as the “Ohkay Owingeh Liquor Control Ordinance.”
Section 2—Purpose
The purpose of this Ordinance is to authorize, regulate, and control the introduction, possession, and Sale of Alcoholic Beverages on Tribal Lands of Ohkay Owingeh in accordance with federal law, New Mexico state law, and the laws of Ohkay Owingeh. The enactment of this Ordinance will enhance the ability of the Tribal government to control all Alcoholic Beverages' related activities within the jurisdiction of the Tribe. This Ordinance is enacted in conjunction with the laws of the State of New Mexico applicable to the Sale and distribution of Alcoholic Beverages pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 1161.
Section 3—Authority
The Tribe enacts this Ordinance pursuant to its inherent governmental powers and in accordance with its traditional law, which empowers its Tribal Council to enact ordinances. This Ordinance conforms with and also has been enacted pursuant to the Act of August 15, 1953 (Pub. L. 83-277, 67 Stat. 586, 18 U.S.C. 1161). The Sale of Alcoholic Beverages shall be lawful within Tribal Lands, to the extent permitted by federal law, and applicable laws of the Tribe and the State of New Mexico.
( printed page 66577)
Section 4—Scope
In order to protect the health, safety, and social welfare of the members of Ohkay Owingeh and the patrons of businesses located on Tribal Lands, and to be consistent with the principles enunciated by the United States Supreme Court in
United States
v.
Montana,
101 S.Ct. 1245 (1981), the Tribe, as an exercise of sovereign authority and self-determination, has enacted this Ordinance to regulate the introduction, possession, and Sale of Alcoholic Beverages on Tribal Lands.
This Ordinance applies to all Tribal Lands, as defined herein. This Ordinance shall extend to all Persons, as defined herein, receiving or requiring Licenses hereunder, or doing business on Tribal Lands, or having significant contacts within Tribal Lands, or residing within Tribal Lands, or entering into or coming within Tribal Lands, or consuming, possessing, manufacturing, or distributing Alcoholic Beverages within Tribal Lands. This Ordinance shall apply to all Persons and shall be enforced against all Persons to the fullest extent permitted by applicable federal law.
Section 5—Definitions

(a) “Alcoholic Beverage” means the four varieties of liquor commonly referred to as alcohol, spirits, wine and beer, and all fermented, spirituous, vinous or malt liquors or combinations thereof, mixed liquor, any part of which is fermented, spirituous, vinous or malt liquor, or any otherwise intoxicating liquid, including every liquid or solid or semi-solid or other substance, patented or not, containing alcohol, spirits, wine or beer and intended for oral consumption;
(b) “Gaming Facility” means all buildings or structures in which Class II or Class III Gaming is conducted on Tribal Lands, subject to the limitations set forth in the Compact between the State of New Mexico and the Tribe.
(c) “Intoxicated Person” means a Person whose mental or physical functioning is impaired as a result of the use of Alcoholic Beverages.
(d) “License” means a revocable license granted by the Tribal Council pursuant to this Ordinance authorizing the Licensee named therein to sell Alcoholic Beverages at a specified Licensed Establishment on Tribal Lands.
(e) “Licensee” means the holder of a valid Package License, On-Premises License or Special Event License granted by the Tribal Council.

(g) “Minor” means any Person under the age of twenty-one (21) years.
(h) “On-Premises License” means a License that authorizes the Licensee to store, possess and sell Alcoholic Beverages in open containers for consumption at the Licensed Establishment only.
(i) “Ordinance” means this Ohkay Owingeh Liquor Control Ordinance.

Our regulation for Protection of Military Cargo within the Captain of the Port Zone Puget Sound, WA identifies the security zones for this event in the Blair Waterway and Sitcum Waterway, Commencement Bay, WA. During the enforcement periods, the operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Captain of the Port or a designated representative.
DATES:
The regulations in 33 CFR 165.1321 will be enforced for the security zones identified in the
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
section below for the dates and times specified.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
If you have questions about this notification of enforcement, call or email LT Anthony Pinto, Sector Puget Sound Waterways Management Division, U.S. Coast Guard; telephone 206-217-6051, email
sectorpugetsoundWWM@uscg.mil.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Coast Guard will enforce security zones in 33 CFR 165.1321(c)(1), the Blair Waterway Security Zone, and 165.1321(c)(2), the Sitcum Waterway Security Zone, for the Military Outloads security zones from 12:01 a.m. on October 30, 2026, to 11:59 p.m. on November 01, 2026. This action is being taken to provide for the security of life and vessels on navigable waterways during this 3-day event. Our regulation for Protection of Military Cargo within the Captain of the Port Zone Puget Sound, WA, § 165.1321, specifies the location of the regulated area for the Military Outloads which encompasses portions of the Blair Waterway and Sitcum Waterway, Commencement Bay, WA. During the enforcement periods, as reflected in § 165.1321(d) if you are the operator of a vessel in the regulated area you must comply with directions from the Captain of the Port or any Designated Representative to enter, move within, or exit the security zones. Vessels 20 meters or greater in length should seek permission from the Captain of the Port or a Designated Representative at least four hours in advance. Vessels less than 20 meters in length should seek permission at least one hour in advance. VTS Puget Sound may be reached on VHF channel 14.
